recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a future work-group decision takes up the broader reserved-parameter-name or breaking-rename question; FHIR-27136 itself is already correctly applied.
issue_request: FHIR-27136 was Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. The original request asked to rename the $preferred-id input parameter from id to identifier, but the final decision explicitly retained the operation and input parameter names and only changed the parameter documentation from "provided id" to "provided identifier" with corrected example wording.
initial_application: Commit 25159ea161eaed360cf05d040c52d38e80cdcbac, "vocab r5 changes to naming system", explicitly listed FHIR-27136 and changed source/namingsystem/operationdefinition-NamingSystem-preferred-id.xml from "provided id"/"mary" to "provided identifier"/"e.g." while retaining the id parameter name.
additional_context: NamingSystem is an active resource in source/fhir.ini and source/namingsystem/list-NamingSystem-operations.xml references OperationDefinition/NamingSystem-preferred-id, so the inspected OperationDefinition is in current build scope. The Zulip thread records the original .NET routing-template concern, and Vocabulary WGM Confluence minutes record FHIR-27136 as Not Persuasive with Modification. Later same-file commits FHIR-37674 and FHIR-37449 did not reverse the documentation change.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current OperationDefinition keeps <name value="id"/> and its documentation says "The server parses the provided identifier to see what type it is (e.g. ...)"; the old exact "provided id" sentence is absent.
